title: DAMA Data Management Body of Knowledge (DAMA-DMBOK), 2nd Edition / DMBOK2 Revised Edition (2024)
publication_date: 2nd Edition (year not stated on page); 2.0 Revision launched 2024; DMBOK 3.0 project started 2025
core_concepts: Data Governance at the hub (DAMA Wheel / Evolved Wheel)
engineering_principles: Organises data management into 11 knowledge areas with Data Governance central; defines data management as the development, execution and supervision of plans, policies, programs and practices that deliver, control, protect and enhance the value of data. Related DAMA pages confirm 11 areas and name Data Governance, Data Quality, Data Security, Data Architecture, Metadata Management and Data Integration & Interoperability as especially critical.
practical_examples: DAMA publishes downloadable wheel graphics and 14 context diagrams (incl. Data Modeling and Design, Reference and Master Data, Data Quality Management, Data Handling Ethics, Big Data and Data Science, Data Management Maturity Assessment) at https://dama.org/dmbok2r-infographics/.
why_it_matters: The de facto vocabulary and chapter structure that most enterprise data governance programmes cite; a schema framework should map its naming, modeling and DQ guidance to the Data Modeling & Design, Metadata and Data Quality knowledge areas.
authority_rationale: Official page of the publishing professional body; DMBOK is a recognised book, not a de jure standard.
notes: Page does not enumerate the knowledge areas; the full 11-name list was taken from secondary summaries (Atlan, search-returned). Conflict: one Jan-2026 DAMA article reportedly says 10 areas. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: DAMA DMBOK Revision (DMBOK2 Revised Edition, 2024 maintenance release) — what changed
publication_date: 2024 (release available via Technics Publications by April 2024; CDMP reference from October 2024 per DAMA FAQ)
core_concepts: currency added as data quality dimension
engineering_principles: States that no material changes were made to the overarching framework, knowledge areas or their definitions; refines Data Quality dimension tables with examples, adds a DQ appendix, defines critical data elements explicitly, and links DQ to data modeling, master/reference data, metadata, integration and governance.
practical_examples: Role renames (Interface Developer -> Data Integration Developer); data described as an intangible asset; ISO content moved from section 1.3.5 to an appendix.
why_it_matters: Lets a framework cite DMBOK2R (2024) for structure while knowing the only DQ-relevant delta is the added 'currency' dimension and refined dimension tables.
authority_rationale: Official publisher statement of changes.
notes: Companion FAQ fetched: https://dama.org/dama-dmbok2-revised-edition-faqs/ (revised edition replaces previous version as authoritative resource).

title: The Six Primary Dimensions For Data Quality Assessment (DAMA UK whitepaper, 'Defining Data Quality Dimensions')
publication_date: Original October 2013 (per academic citations); dama-uk.org page shows 4 Apr 2025; image filename references 2020
engineering_principles: Defines six generic best-practice DQ dimensions to reduce confusion; organisations should first agree the quality rules for their data and need not weight dimensions equally (search summary).
practical_examples: Adopted verbatim by the UK Government Data Quality Hub and IBM product documentation.
why_it_matters: Most widely re-used DQ dimension vocabulary; maps directly to schema constraints (validity -> CHECK/domain, uniqueness -> PK/UNIQUE, completeness -> NOT NULL).
authority_rationale: Professional-body whitepaper widely adopted by governments and vendors; full text is members-only so definitions were taken from GOV.UK.
notes: Page is a members-only gate; it names no dimensions. RECOMMENDED. Conflicts with ISO/IEC 25012's 15 characteristics (no 'uniqueness'/'timeliness' by name).

title: Meet the data quality dimensions (UK Government Data Quality Hub)
organization_author: UK Government Data Quality Hub (Office for National Statistics)
engineering_principles: Validity = expected format, type and range (valid is not necessarily accurate); completeness is about critical vs optional data; no single dimension is sufficient; measure regularly because data changes over time.
practical_examples: Government Data Quality Framework; points statistical outputs to the European Statistical System QAF instead.
why_it_matters: Freely readable authoritative restatement of the DAMA UK definitions, usable as the citation for each dimension in a schema framework.
authority_rationale: Official government publication explicitly attributing the dimensions to DAMA UK.
notes: States that organisations may define different dimensions. RECOMMENDED.

title: ISO/IEC 9075-1:2023 Information technology — Database languages SQL — Part 1: Framework (SQL/Framework)
core_concepts: optional features identified by feature IDs
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue (search summary): defines the conceptual framework, terms and notation used by the other parts; 2023 edition adds terms/concepts to support new data types required by incremental parts. SQL:2023 parts named: Framework, Foundation, SQL/CLI, SQL/PSM, SQL/MED, SQL/OLB, SQL/Schemata, SQL/JRT, SQL/XML, SQL/PGQ (Part 16).
practical_examples: SQL:2023 new features: JSON type (T801), enhanced JSON (T802), SQL/PGQ graph queries over tables, GREATEST/LEAST (T054), ANY_VALUE (T626), underscores in numeric literals (T662), UNIQUE null treatment (F292).
why_it_matters: The only international standard for the database language itself; precise citations should use part number, edition year and feature ID (e.g., ISO/IEC 9075-2:2023 feature T801).
authority_rationale: International standard; BSI is the UK national body mirror of the ISO catalogue entry.
notes: ISO page https://www.iso.org/standard/76583.html returned 403 (search-returned). Part list and feature IDs from Wikipedia SQL:2023 (fetched) citing Eisentraut's 4 Apr 2023 post (URL 404). Part 15 SQL/MDA not confirmed. Paywalled per part. RECOMMENDED where features are standardised.

title: Temporal features in SQL:2011 (SIGMOD Record 41(3), September 2012)
core_concepts: PERIOD FOR as table metadata, no period data type
FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF / FROM..TO / BETWEEN..AND
engineering_principles: Periods are defined as named metadata over a pair of conventional datetime columns because adding a PERIOD type would need support across JDBC/ODBC/.NET, ETL and replication; closed-open semantics with implied end>start constraint; system-period columns are GENERATED ALWAYS and set from the transaction timestamp so history cannot be tampered with; at most one application-time and one system-time period per table; default query returns current rows.
practical_examples: CREATE TABLE Emp(... PERIOD FOR SYSTEM_TIME (Sys_start, Sys_end)) WITH SYSTEM VERSIONING; ALTER TABLE Emp ADD PRIMARY KEY (ENo, EPeriod WITHOUT OVERLAPS); UPDATE Emp FOR PORTION OF EPeriod FROM DATE '2011-02-03' TO DATE '2011-09-10' SET EDept = 4 WHERE ENo = 22217; SELECT ... FROM Emp FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF TIMESTAMP '2011-01-02 00:00:00'.
why_it_matters: Primary account by the standard's authors of how temporal/bitemporal tables are standardised in ISO/IEC 9075-2; directly governs audit-history and effective-dating schema patterns.
authority_rationale: Written by members of the ISO SQL committee and published in ACM SIGMOD Record; the closest open primary source to the paywalled standard.
notes: Text extracted from the fetched PDF with pypdf. Authors note commercial adoption had been slow (one implementation in 2012). RECOMMENDED pattern.

title: What's New in SQL:2016 (modern-sql.com)
engineering_principles: SQL:2016 has no native JSON type; JSON is stored as strings and processed by functions; a JSON type arrived only in ISO/IEC 9075-2:2023 (feature T801).
practical_examples: JSON_TABLE to shred JSON documents into relational rows; LISTAGG as ordered-set string aggregation.
why_it_matters: Clarifies that JSON column typing was vendor-specific until 2023, which affects schema portability decisions for semi-structured columns.
authority_rationale: Well-known SQL practitioner closely tracking the ISO standard; not a standards body.
notes: OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL for JSON features.

title: ISO/IEC 11179-5:2015 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 5: Naming principles
core_concepts: principles and rules for developing naming conventions
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: provides instruction for naming concepts, data element concepts, conceptual domains, data elements and value domains as defined in ISO/IEC 11179-3; describes naming in metadata registries; gives principles and rules for developing naming conventions and example conventions.
practical_examples: Secondary sources (Wikipedia 'Representation term', DDI Alliance guide, a US state naming standard) describe the associated object-class-term + property-term + representation-term (+ qualifier) convention, e.g., EmployeeAddressText; representation terms (class words) such as Amount, Code, Date, Identifier, Indicator, Name, Text.
why_it_matters: The only international standard directly about naming data elements; a schema framework should cite it as the authority for having a documented naming convention with class words, while presenting the concrete pattern as 'aligned with' rather than 'required by' the standard.
authority_rationale: International standard; IEC webstore shows the official abstract.
notes: 25 pages; webstore showed 'CHF 0.-' (likely display artefact; treat as paywalled). Draft 4th edition: https://www.iso.org/standard/92786.html (search-returned). Abstract does not mention object class/property/representation term. RECOMMENDED (convention), OPTIONAL (specific pattern).

title: ISO/IEC 11179-3:2023 Information technology — Metadata registries (MDR) — Part 3: Metamodel for registry common facilities
engineering_principles: Defines the information a metadata registry should record as a conceptual data model (search summary of SCC/Genorma listings): Clause 6 core model with reusable basic types and classes; Clauses 7-11 identification, designation/definition, registration, classification, mapping.
practical_examples: Registries built on 11179: NCI caDSR, AIHW METeOR, USHIK, Aristotle Metadata Registry (Wikipedia, fetched).
why_it_matters: Reference model for the metadata/data-dictionary layer of a schema framework (how data elements, value domains and definitions are registered and versioned).
authority_rationale: International standard (ISO catalogue URL returned verbatim by search).
notes: iso.org returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool; details from search summaries (97 pages, paid). Earlier title 'Registry metamodel and basic attributes' belongs to the 2003/2013 editions. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Software engineering — SQuaRE — Data quality model
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: general data quality model for data retained in a structured format within a computer system; usable to establish DQ requirements, define measures, and plan/perform evaluations (incl. compliance with legislation). Verified definitions (iso25000.com): accuracy = attributes correctly represent the true value (syntactic and semantic); completeness = values for all expected attributes and related entity instances; consistency = free from contradiction and coherent with other data.
practical_examples: Inherent characteristics map to schema constraints and provenance columns; system-dependent ones (availability, recoverability, portability) map to platform controls.
why_it_matters: The international DQ vocabulary against which DAMA/DAMA UK dimensions must be reconciled; cite as ISO/IEC 25012:2008 with 25024 for measures.
authority_rationale: International standard; IEC webstore shows official abstract.
notes: 13 pages, CHF 100. The full 15-item list with inherent/system-dependent mapping was not verifiable from an opened source (paywalled; secondary pages show it only as images). RECOMMENDED. Conflicts with DAMA UK six-dimension vocabulary.

title: ISO/IEC 25024:2015 Systems and software engineering — SQuaRE — Measurement of data quality
core_concepts: target entities across data life cycle
structured data in legacy systems, data warehouses, the web
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: basic set of measures for each 25012 characteristic, target entities, guidance on applying measures and on defining organisation-specific measures; explicitly does not define value ranges for grading; excludes knowledge representation, data mining and statistical significance.
practical_examples: Reported annexes (search summary): quality measure elements, alphabetical list of measures, table of measures by characteristic and target entity.
why_it_matters: Gives a standards-based way to express DQ metrics (e.g., completeness ratio of a column) in a schema framework without inventing thresholds.
authority_rationale: International standard; official abstract on IEC webstore.
notes: 45 pages, CHF 181. ISO page https://www.iso.org/standard/35749.html search-returned. RECOMMENDED.

title: ISO 8000-61:2016 Data quality — Part 61: Data quality management: Process reference model
core_concepts: implementation processes: planning, control, assurance, improvement
relationship between DQ management and data governance
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue (search summary): specifies the processes required for data quality management, each defined by purpose, outcomes and activities; covers principles, process structure, lower-level processes, relationship to data governance and implementation requirements; used to assess process capability or organisational maturity.
practical_examples: Applies to structured data in databases and to less structured data (images, audio, video, documents); process groups: Implementation (plan/control/assurance/improvement), Data-Related Support (architecture, transfer, operations, security), Resource Provision (organisation, human resources).
why_it_matters: Standardised process vocabulary for the DQ operating model that sits around a schema (planning, control, assurance, improvement).
authority_rationale: International standard; DIN Media is the German national-body listing.
notes: 21 pages, EUR 154.60 PDF, ICS 25.040.40. DIN page shows no abstract; scope and structure from search summaries (iteh.es DNS failure; ANSI preview 403). OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: ISO 8000-110:2021 Data quality — Part 110: Master data: Exchange of characteristic data: Syntax, semantic encoding, and conformance to data specification
core_concepts: computer-checkable requirements for master data messages
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue (search summary): requirements for exchange of messages containing characteristic master data that can be checked by computer, plus requirements on access to the data dictionaries used to decode them; 'necessary but not sufficient' for master-data quality; accuracy handled by ISO 8000-130.
practical_examples: Exchange formats cited: ISO 9735 (EDIFACT), ISO 13584, ISO 15926, ISO 22745 series.
why_it_matters: Relevant to master-data and reference-data schema design in industrial supply chains where characteristic data must be dictionary-encoded.
authority_rationale: International standard (ISO catalogue URL returned verbatim by search).
notes: iso.org 403 on fetch; CHF 135; page count disputed between resellers (20 vs 30). OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: ISO/IEC 38505-1 Information technology — Governance of IT — Governance of data — Part 1: Application of ISO/IEC 38500 to the governance of data
core_concepts: governance of data for governing bodies
ISO/IEC 38500 principles and model applied to data
data created, collected, stored or controlled by IT systems
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: guiding principles for members of governing bodies on effective, efficient and acceptable use of data; applies ISO/IEC 38500 to data; helps stakeholders gain confidence; establishes a data governance vocabulary; implementation guidance for IT governance is in ISO/IEC/TS 38501.
practical_examples: Positions data governance as a domain within IT governance within corporate governance (search summary).
why_it_matters: The ISO-level definition of data governance that a framework can cite for accountability principles above the schema; note the 2026 edition supersedes 2017.
authority_rationale: International standard; Genorma mirrors the ISO status record.
notes: 2026 edition catalogue page https://www.iso.org/standard/87195.html (search-returned; 403 on fetch); changes in 2026 edition not visible. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Information security, cybersecurity and privacy protection — Information security management systems — Requirements
core_concepts: Annex A controls (93 in 4 themes per vendor summaries)
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an ISMS and for assessing and treating information security risks; 'Excluding any of the requirements specified in Clauses 4 to 10 is not acceptable when an organization claims conformity.'
practical_examples: Vendor summaries (not the abstract) describe 93 Annex A controls: Organizational 37, People 8, Physical 14, Technological 34; 11 new controls incl. threat intelligence, cloud services security; selection is risk-based.
why_it_matters: Sets the control context for data classification, access control and logging requirements that schemas must support (e.g., sensitivity labels, audit columns).
authority_rationale: International standard; official abstract on IEC webstore.
notes: 19 pages, CHF 155. ISO page https://www.iso.org/standard/27001 search-returned. MANDATORY (Clauses 4-10) only when conformity/certification is claimed; Annex A controls risk-selected.

title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
organization_author: ISO/TC 46/SC 11 (listing by Estonian Centre for Standardisation, EVS)
publication_date: 2016-04 (valid from 07.04.2016); ISO reports reviewed and confirmed 2021
core_concepts: processes for creating, capturing and managing records
engineering_principles: Scope per ISO catalogue: concepts and principles from which approaches to creation, capture and management of records are developed; applies to records in any business or technological environment over time.
practical_examples: Companion ISO/TR 15489-2 gives procedures (search summary); publisher summaries say the 2016 revision dropped a prescribed methodology and emphasised risk.
why_it_matters: Basis for retention/disposition and records-metadata attributes in schemas where rows are legal records.
authority_rationale: International standard; EVS is a national-body mirror.
notes: EUR 206.76 at EVS. The abstract does not mention retention or disposition explicitly. ISO page https://www.iso.org/standard/62542.html search-returned. RECOMMENDED where data constitutes records.

title: DCAM — Data Management Capability Assessment Model (v3)
core_concepts: Business Data Knowledge component (new in v3)
engineering_principles: Capabilities are scored on whether the right people with authority participate (Engagement), how established and repeatable processes are (Process), and auditable artefacts (Evidence); v3 consolidates architecture capabilities into one component.
practical_examples: Case studies: Standard Bank, Nationwide, Novartis, Entain, McDonald's; members receive a read-only DCAM modelling tool.
why_it_matters: Industry (financial services origin) maturity model that audits whether data architecture/model and DQ capabilities exist; useful as an assessment layer over a schema framework.
authority_rationale: Major industry association's official framework page; proprietary and members-only, not a standards body.
notes: Page does not name all eight components or prices. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: DGI Data Governance Framework — Framework Components
organization_author: Data Governance Institute (founder/primary author Gwen Thomas)
publication_date: n.d. (framework online since 2003 per secondary sources; page © 2026)
engineering_principles: Ten universal components answering why/what/who/how of governance; decision rights must precede rule creation; a Data Governance Office facilitates and supports governance and stewardship.
practical_examples: Data products such as glossaries with data definitions and metadata are explicit framework outputs.
why_it_matters: Free, long-standing framework that supplies the accountability/decision-rights vocabulary (owner, steward, DGO) a schema framework needs for ownership metadata.
authority_rationale: Well-known practitioner institute; widely cited but not a standards body.
notes: 'All Rights Reserved'; author not stated on page. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: ISO 3166 — Country Codes (Parts 1-3, 2020 editions)
engineering_principles: Codes, not names, identify countries; names come from UN sources; alpha-2 recommended for general use; subdivision code = country alpha-2 + separator + up to three alphanumerics; codes are maintained and changed by a Maintenance Agency.
practical_examples: Country reference table keyed by alpha-2 with alpha-3 and numeric columns, effective-dated to handle retirements (ISO 3166-3).
why_it_matters: Standard code set for country columns and FK reference tables; the free-use statement removes licensing concerns for embedding code lists.
authority_rationale: Standards body page (URL returned verbatim by search; 403 on fetch).
notes: Part 1 catalogue: https://www.iso.org/standard/72482.html (search-returned). Content from search summaries of iso.org. RECOMMENDED.

title: ISO 4217 Currency Codes — Maintenance Agency lists (SIX)
organization_author: SIX Group (Secretariat of the ISO 4217 Maintenance Agency, on behalf of ISO and SNV)
publication_date: n.d. (lists updated by amendment; latest shown effective 2026-01-01)
core_concepts: List One current currencies and funds (XLS/XML)
engineering_principles: Lists change when a currency is created, withdrawn or altered; each entry carries Entity, Currency, Alphabetic Code, Numeric Code and Minor Unit (number of decimal places), published free of charge in machine-readable form.
practical_examples: Amendment effective 1 Jan 2026: Bulgaria adopts EUR (978, minor unit 2); BGN (975, minor unit 2) moves to List Three; fixed rate EUR 1 = BGN 1.95583; dual price display 08.08.2025-08.08.2026.
why_it_matters: Minor Unit is the authoritative source for per-currency decimal scale of monetary amounts; because it changes via amendments, scale should be data-driven from the list rather than hard-coded.
authority_rationale: Official Maintenance Agency publication of the ISO 4217 code lists.
notes: ISO's own ISO 4217 page returned 403. RECOMMENDED.

title: ISO 8601-1:2019 Date and time — Representations for information interchange — Part 1: Basic rules
organization_author: ISO/TC 154 (Processes, data elements and documents in commerce, industry and administration), WG5
publication_date: 2019-03-25 (stage 90.92, under revision); Amd 1:2022 and Part 2 'Extensions' (8601-2:2019) reported by search
core_concepts: composite date-time elements as character strings
engineering_principles: Scope: representations of Gregorian dates and 24-hour times and composites as character strings for interchange, incl. times and time shifts based on UTC; excludes non-Gregorian calendars and non-24-hour clocks; does not address character encoding (search summary).
practical_examples: API/export date-time strings; Part 2 extensions (EDTF-style uncertain/approximate dates) per search.
why_it_matters: Governs serialized date/time formats at schema boundaries (CSV/JSON exports, API contracts); database column types are vendor-defined and out of scope.
authority_rationale: Page of the responsible ISO technical committee.
notes: ISO store ID 70907; iso.org pages 403. RECOMMENDED for interchange.

title: ISO 639:2023 Code for individual languages and language groups
organization_author: ISO / ISO 639 Maintenance Agency (Infoterm, Library of Congress, SIL International as Language Coding Agencies)
core_concepts: Set 3 three-letter identifiers for all individual languages
harmonised terminology and principles of language coding
engineering_principles: Specifies the language code and rules for choosing, forming and using language identifiers; excludes reconstructed and formal languages (search summary).
practical_examples: Language columns using Set 1 (ISO 639-1 style 'en') or Set 3 ('eng') with a reference table loaded from the Language Coding Agencies.
why_it_matters: Standard code set for language/locale columns; the 2023 consolidation changes how the standard should be cited (ISO 639:2023 Set N, not 639-N).
authority_rationale: Standards body page (URL returned verbatim by search; not fetched).
notes: SCC listing https://scc-ccn.ca/standardsdb/standards/8184254 (search-returned). Publication date reported as 1 or 8 Nov 2023 by different stores. RECOMMENDED.

title: ISO 20022 Repository — Data Dictionary and Business Process Catalogue
publication_date: n.d. (ISO 20022-1:2004 withdrawn; ISO 20022-1:2026 reported, series of nine parts, April 2026 — unverified)
engineering_principles: Repository has two parts: Data Dictionary (reusable Business Concepts, Message Concepts, Data Types under release control) and Business Process Catalogue (message models with XML/ASN.1 schemas); free access for users and developers (search summaries of iso20022.org).
practical_examples: Message domains with Message Definition Reports and Usage Guides; 2025 paper on generating JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 from ISO 20022.
why_it_matters: A free, governed business-concept and data-type dictionary that financial schemas can reuse for element names and types.
authority_rationale: Official Registration Authority site and ISO catalogue (URLs returned by search; site returned 403/404 to fetch).
notes: ISO 20022-1:2004 catalogue https://www.iso.org/standard/40337.html (search-returned). Conflict: part count eight (older FAQ) vs nine (2026). MANDATORY only where a payment scheme mandates ISO 20022 messaging (not verified here).

title: ISO 17442: The LEI Code Structure (GLEIF)
publication_date: n.d. (ISO 17442 Part 1 published 2012; Part 2 2019; GLEIF established 2014)
core_concepts: Global LEI Index with reference data incl. ownership
engineering_principles: Four ISO 17442 principles: global standard, single unique identifier per legal entity, backed by high-quality data, free public good; overseen by the Regulatory Oversight Committee, backed by G20/FSB.
practical_examples: Example LEI 506700GE1G29325QX363; mandates: CFTC rule (2013), EMIR (2012), MiFID II/MiFIR (2018), RBI cross-border transactions (2021), Korea FSC (2023), Japan FSA OTC derivatives (2024).
why_it_matters: The only identifier in this set that regulators require in named reporting contexts; legal-entity tables should carry an LEI column (CHAR(20)) validated against the Global LEI Index.
authority_rationale: Operating body of the Global LEI System designated under ISO 17442.
notes: Page does not describe prefix/check-digit structure or the ISO 17442-1:2020 edition. MANDATORY in listed regulatory contexts; RECOMMENDED elsewhere.

title: The ANSI/X3/SPARC DBMS framework report of the study group on database management systems (Information Systems 3(3), 1978)
organization_author: Dennis Tsichritzis, Anthony Klug (for ANSI/X3/SPARC Study Group); Elsevier
engineering_principles: Separation of user views (external), the single enterprise conceptual schema, and physical storage (internal) to achieve logical and physical data independence (architecture content from secondary sources; bibliographic record verified).
practical_examples: Modern conceptual -> logical -> physical model progression and view layers in databases are the descendants of this framework.
why_it_matters: Foundational citation for separating conceptual, logical and physical schema layers; never became a formal standard.
authority_rationale: Peer-reviewed journal publication of the study group's report; DOI 10.1016/0306-4379(78)90001-7 verified via Crossref.
notes: 1975 Interim Report (FDT/ACM SIGMOD Bulletin 7(2)) known only via Wikipedia (search-returned); DTIC copy returned 403. RECOMMENDED principle.

title: The entity-relationship model: toward a unified view of data (Chen, 1976)
organization_author: Peter P. S. Chen; MIT Sloan School of Management (Working Paper 839-76); journal version ACM TODS 1(1):9-36
core_concepts: derivation of network, relational and entity-set models
engineering_principles: A data model that incorporates semantic information about the real world plus a diagramming technique for database design; shows network, relational and entity-set models can be derived from a common base (search snippet of abstract).
practical_examples: ER diagrams as the conceptual-model notation in virtually all schema design methods.
why_it_matters: Foundational peer-reviewed source for conceptual modeling; cite as ACM TODS 1(1), 1976, DOI 10.1145/320434.320440.
authority_rationale: Foundational peer-reviewed paper; MIT DSpace record fetched; ACM page returned 403.
notes: Open scanned copy fetched (image-only PDF): https://www.comp.nus.edu.sg/~lingtw/papers/tods76.chen.pdf. Presented earlier at VLDB 1975.

title: FIPS PUB 184 — Integration Definition for Information Modeling (IDEF1X)
organization_author: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Computer Systems Laboratory; approved by the Secretary of Commerce
core_concepts: application-independent view transformable into physical design
engineering_principles: Describes the IDEF1X language and rules for developing a logical model of data to support management of data as a resource, integration of information systems and building of databases; objective (d): an application-independent view of data validated by users and transformed into a physical database design; based on ICAM IISS Vol. V Part 4 (1985).
practical_examples: Waiver procedure (section 12) shows it was binding on federal agencies; IDEF1X notation survives in ERwin-style key-based diagrams; successor ISO/IEC/IEEE 31320-2:2012.
why_it_matters: The only government-mandated (historically) data modeling notation standard; useful precedent for logical-to-physical transformation rules.
authority_rationale: Official NIST publication (161 pages) fetched from NIST's archive; text extracted with pypdf.
notes: Was MANDATORY for US federal agencies 1994-2008; now OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL. Withdrawal date from Wikipedia (search-returned).

title: ISO/IEC 19505-1:2012 Information technology — Object Management Group Unified Modeling Language (OMG UML) — Part 1: Infrastructure
organization_author: ISO/IEC JTC 1 (listing by IEC webstore); OMG
engineering_principles: Establishes UML 2 for system architects, software engineers and developers for analysis, design and implementation of software-based systems and for modeling business processes (abstract).
practical_examples: UML class diagrams used as conceptual/logical data models and for ISO/IEC 19763 metamodels.
why_it_matters: Gives a standards-body citation for using class-diagram notation in data modeling; 220 pages, CHF 227.
authority_rationale: International standard; official abstract on IEC webstore.
notes: Part 2 (Superstructure) not shown on page. ISO page https://www.iso.org/standard/32624.html search-returned. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: OMG Common Warehouse Metamodel (CWM) Specification, Version 1.1
core_concepts: relational, multidimensional, OLAP, transformation, data mining packages
engineering_principles: Proposes XMI to exchange data warehouse metadata based on a CWM metamodel specified with MOF; modules cover relational, multidimensional, OLAP, transformation and data mining.
practical_examples: Legacy ETL/BI tool metadata exchange; machine-readable files on the page are labelled CWM 1.0.
why_it_matters: Formal (if dated) standard metamodel for warehouse schema metadata; relevant when citing lineage between relational and OLAP models.
authority_rationale: Official OMG specification page.
notes: No ISO adoption mentioned on the page. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL (no update since 2003).

title: Data Catalog Vocabulary (DCAT) — Version 3, W3C Recommendation
engineering_principles: RDF vocabulary enabling interoperable data catalogs; standard model for describing datasets and data services so metadata can be aggregated and discovered; Catalog is a sub-class of Dataset; distributions carry accessURL/downloadURL/byteSize/mediaType/checksum.
practical_examples: Properties dcat:dataset, dcat:distribution, dcat:endpointURL, dcat:servesDataset, dcat:version, dcat:previousVersion, dcat:hasCurrentVersion, dcat:temporalResolution, dcat:spatialResolutionInMeters.
why_it_matters: De jure web standard for dataset-level metadata in data catalogs; schema frameworks should emit DCAT for table/dataset registration.
authority_rationale: W3C Recommendation (standards body).
notes: Only the first ~100k characters were read. RECOMMENDED for published dataset metadata.

title: OpenLineage specification and object model
organization_author: OpenLineage project (Linux Foundation / LF AI & Data; Technical Steering Committee)
publication_date: n.d. (docs version 1.55.0; LF AI & Data project page last updated 2024-06-18)
core_concepts: Dataset (name within datasource namespace, e.g., db.host.database.schema.table)
facets (schema, dataSource, version, dataQualityMetrics, dataQualityAssertions, outputStatistics, sql, parent)
engineering_principles: Spec formalised as a JSON Schema with extension via custom facets; a run needs a START and a COMPLETE/FAIL/ABORT event; facet _schemaURL must be immutable and canonical; custom facets carry a project prefix; emitting a facet with the same name replaces the previous one.
practical_examples: Dataset schema facet and column-level lineage emitted by Airflow/Spark/dbt integrations (integrations named generically on the site).
why_it_matters: De facto interchange shape for physical schema and lineage metadata between tools; not a standards-body standard.
authority_rationale: Official project documentation of a widely adopted open-source LF specification.
notes: Also fetched: https://github.com/OpenLineage/OpenLineage/blob/main/spec/OpenLineage.md, https://openlineage.io/, https://lfaidata.foundation/projects/openlineage/ (body not rendered). The brief's https://openlineage.io/spec/ returned 404. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.

title: Data Model Scorecard: Applying the Industry Standard on Data Model Quality
publication_date: n.d. on page (ISBN-13 9781634620826 in cover filename; earlier TDAN columns 2006-2008)
engineering_principles: Ten-category scorecard for rating data model quality (requirements capture, completeness, appropriate scheme e.g. relational vs dimensional, structural soundness, abstraction level, naming/standards compliance, readability, definitions, enterprise consistency, metadata-matches-data).
practical_examples: Applied in Hoberman's consulting reviews of client models; category wording differs between 2006 TDAN articles and the book.
why_it_matters: The most commonly cited model-review checklist in DAMA circles; a practitioner method, not a standard despite the subtitle.
authority_rationale: Recognised book by a well-known data modeling author/publisher.
notes: Reference in DMBOK chapter on Data Modeling & Design is widely reported but not verified from an opened DAMA page. OPTIONAL/CONTEXTUAL.
